Native figure and table numbering with knitr hooks

Source: vignettes/numbering-hook.Rmd
numbering-hook.Rmd

Quarto numbers figures and tables as static text (“Figure 1”) and resolves @fig-x references to static text too. oq_numbering() gives the figures and tables created by R chunks real Word captions instead: Figure <SEQ field>: caption, wrapped in a bookmark named after the chunk label. Word computes the numbers itself and renumbers when you insert or move items.

This is an opt-in alternative to the post-render option officequarto.crossref.auto-number (vignette("options")), which converts Quarto’s finished static captions afterwards. The two differ in where they act:

oq_numbering() (this vignette) crossref.auto-number
Acts while knitting (knitr hooks) after rendering (on the docx)
Reference syntax @fig-x (converted by the extension), or `r oq_ref(“fig-x”)` @fig-x
Covers figures/tables from R chunks any Quarto-numbered caption
Customisable your own hook function fixed

Setup

Call it once in the setup chunk, after loading the package (hooks only exist inside the R session that knits the document):

library(officequarto)
oq_numbering()

Then write figures and tables as usual, with a fig-/tbl- label and a caption:

```{r}
#| label: fig-sales
#| fig-cap: "Sales by region"
plot(sales)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-top
#| tbl-cap: "Top *five* customers"
knitr::kable(head(customers, 5))
```

As `r oq_ref("fig-sales")` and `r oq_ref("tbl-top")` show, ...

Referencing

In an officequarto project (project: type: officequarto) write Quarto’s usual notation: @fig-sales, [@fig-sales], [@fig-sales; @tbl-top], [see @fig-sales, p. 3]. The extension’s refs.lua filter finds the captions built by oq_numbering() and turns the matching citations into clickable Word REF fields that display the label and number (“Figure 1”). Citations to anything else (native Quarto figures and tables, literature, unknown ids) are left to Quarto, also inside a mixed citation.

oq_ref("fig-sales") produces the same field from inline R. It is the fallback when the extension is not active, and for other output formats it returns @fig-sales, so the same document still renders to HTML.

Label text and separator

The label, separator and (for tables) caption style are chunk options, so they can be set once for the whole project in _quarto.yml:

knitr:
  opts_chunk:
    oq.fig.label: "Abbildung"
    oq.tbl.label: "Tabelle"
    oq.sep: ": "
    oq.tbl.style: "Table Caption"   # display name of the caption paragraph style

or overridden in a single chunk (#| oq.fig.label: "Plate"). Table captions may contain inline markdown.

A custom hook

fig_hook and tbl_hook replace the built-in post-processing. They are still chained onto Quarto’s own hooks, so they receive what Quarto produced and return the markdown to use instead:

  • fig_hook(res, options) — res is the image markdown from Quarto’s plot hook: ![caption](path){#fig-id width=...}.
  • tbl_hook(res, options) — res is the whole cell markdown from Quarto’s chunk hook: ::: {#tbl-id .cell tbl-cap='...'} ....

options is the list of chunk options (options$label, options$fig.cap, your own oq.* options, …). The defaults are available as oq_fig_hook() and oq_tbl_hook(), so a custom hook can extend them instead of starting from scratch:

oq_numbering(
  fig_hook = function(res, options) {
    paste0(oq_fig_hook()(res, options), "\n\nSource: ", options$source, "\n\n")
  }
)

A custom hook that builds its own captions is responsible for the cross-reference id (drop #fig-id from the image attributes, as the default does, if you do not want Quarto to number the figure as well) and for unique bookmark names if you want oq_ref() to point at them.

Limits

  • Only R-chunk figures and tables are handled (label starting with fig-/tbl- plus fig-cap/tbl-cap). Markdown images and tables, sub-figures (fig-subcap) and layout chunks are left to Quarto.
  • Quarto no longer knows the numbered items, so its own @fig-x handling does not apply to them: they are resolved by the extension’s refs.lua filter, or by oq_ref() without the extension. There is no list of figures or tables.
  • Output other than docx is passed through unchanged.
  • With officequarto.crossref.auto-number: true the hook-owned captions are skipped by the post-render conversion (no double conversion; checked in the test fixture).

Mixing with native Quarto figures and tables

Native items (markdown images and tables with a #fig-/#tbl- id) keep Quarto’s numbering, which is static text (“Figure 1”). Hook-numbered items are live SEQ fields, so without further settings both can show the same number. Turn on officequarto.crossref.auto-number: true in that case: it converts the native captions to SEQ fields in the same sequence, so hook-numbered and native items count together, and @fig-x works for both kinds. Make the label text agree as well — the hook uses oq.fig.label / oq.tbl.label, the native captions use Quarto’s crossref: fig-title / tbl-title — otherwise one item reads “Abbildung 1” and the next “Figure 2”. - Table captions go in the paragraph style Table Caption (oq.tbl.style); your reference-doc should define it, otherwise Pandoc’s fallback style is pruned and Word’s default is used.
